## Order Inventory Batch Location Assignment

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/order-batch-location-assignment

The Product Expiration Dates app allows you to configure when inventory batches are assigned to an order: either when the order is placed or, when an order line is fulfilled. See [Adding Expiration Data to Products](https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/adding-expiration-data).

By default a product's soonest expiring inventory batch from across all locations is assigned to the order line (FEFO: First Expired, First Out management strategy) If the incoming order has a location assigned (typically [Shopify Point of Sale (POS) orders](https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/pos-integration)), that location will be used. You can change your management strategy to First In, First Out (FIFO) management strategy on the settings' page Inventory tab.

## Shopify Order Routing Rules

***Support for Shopify Order Routing Rules is only available under the Pro Plan***

To assign an inventory batch from a location determined by Shopify Order Routing rules select "Assign inventory batches based on Shopify Order Routing" from the Settings page's Inventory tab. Shopify Order Routing can be configured in the Shopify Admin here

## Assign Inventory Batches from a Specific Location

**Do not set this if you use [prioritized fulfillment locations](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/locations/setting-up-your-location-fulfillments#set-locations-for-order-fulfillment-priority).**

If you're using "order placed" for a Product's ["Assign inventory batches when"](https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/adding-expiration-data) setting and have multiple locations in Shopify **but only fulfill from one**, you must set "Assign inventory batches from this location" to match your default location in Shopify (Shopify does not share this with 3rd-party apps so it must be explicitly set). When this is set and an order is placed without a location the Product Expiration Dates app will only allocate the soonest expirting expiration date from this location. If this is not set the app will allocate the soonest expiring expiration date across all locations.

---

## Inventory Transfers

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/inventory-transfers

***Inventory transfer support is only available under the Premium and Platinum plans***

To enable support for [Shopify inventory transfers](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/inventory/inventory-transfers):

-   Go to the Inventory tab on the settings page
-   Check "Move inventory batches when Shopify inventory transfers occur"
-   Click "Update"

Now when an inventory transfer occurs in Shopify inventory batches for the tranfered quantity will be moved from the transfer's source location to its destination location. Quantities are moved starting with the soonest expiring inventory batch. If you need a different algorithm contact support.

---

## Inventory Push

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/inventory-push

***Inventory push is only available under the Pro Plan***

Inventory push makes the Product Expiration Dates app the "source of truth" for your store's inventory, preventing you from having to enter the inventory in the Shopify Admin, then re-enter it with its expiration date/quantity breakdown in the app.

With inventory push enabled you [enter your inventory quantities](https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/adding-expiration-data) once in the Product Expiration Dates app and it will adjust the products' inventory counts in Shopify. When quantities in the app are added, updated, or deleted, the app will make the appropriate adjustments in Shopify.

Changes to product inventory via an new order or an order status change (refunded, restocked, etc...) are part of the Product Expiration Date app's default behavior. **A Pro plan subscription is not required for this to work.**

When inventory push is enabled **inventory must only be entered into the Product Expiration Dates app. Do not modify inventory via the Shopify Admin**. Values entered into the Shopify Admin will not be seen by the app because expiration dates and/or batch numbers cannot be entered into the Shopify Admin. For example, if you entered the following data in the Product Expiration Dates app for Product A:

-   Expires: `2021-11-10`, Quantity: `7`
-   Expires: `2022-01-01`, Quantity: `12`

These value will be pushed to Shopify and you will see a total **available** quantity of 19 in the Shopify Admin. If you change this to 30 in the Shopify Admin, the Product Expiration Dates app does not know what date(s) the new 11 must be associated with. Are they November 10th, January 1st, or something else? This is why inventory push cannot sync quantities entered into the Shopify Admin.

## Enabling

1.  Make sure you're subscribed to the Pro Plan or higher
2.  Visit the settings page
3.  Select "Push edits made to inventory batch quantities to Shopify"
4.  Click the Update button to save your settings

In order to push inventory to Shopify expiration dates must have their location set.

## Available and On Hand Quantities

By default Inventory Push sets the available quantity in Shopify. If you're subscribed to the the Premium plan you can configure it to set on hand quantities instead. This can be done from the settings page's Inventory tab by selecting "Set on hand quantity instead of available quantity".

## Inventory Batch Assignment

When using Inventory Push you cannot [assign inventory batches to a product](https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/adding-expiration-data) when an order line is fulfilled. Only when an order is placed. This is due to how Shopify manages inventory quantities. They assign them to an order line when it is placed. Let's look at an example below.

If you enter a 10 quantity into the app, we assign 10 to the available quantity in Shopify. When an order is placed for a quantity of 2, Shopify reduces the quantity to 8, but in the app this quantity remains 10 until the product is fulfilled. If you then go into the app before this occurs and enter a quantity of 12, we will update Shopify's available quantity to 12, which would be incorrect.

## Variants

When inventory push in enabled for a product with variants, any variant for the product that has not been entered in to the Product Expiration Dates app will have its inventory set to 0 in Shopify.

## Bundles

Pushing inventory bundles will set the bundle's quantity as well as the quantities of the products it contains. For example, given the following products:

| Product | SKU | Inventory Available |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product A | X123 | 5 |
| Product B | Y456 | 10 |

If you create a bundle contianing these products with the following configuration:

| Product | SKU | Bundled Quantity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product A | X123 | 1 |
| Product B | Y456 | 3 |

It results in the following:

| Product | SKU | Inventory Available |
| --- | --- | --- |
| My Bundle | B999 | 3 |
| Product A | X123 | 5 |
| Product B | Y456 | 10 |

The bundle's quantity is set to the minimum quantity that can be purchased based on the quantities of the products it bundles. If a customer made a purchase of Product B with a quantity of 6, the inventories would be synced to the following:

| Product | SKU | Inventory Available |
| --- | --- | --- |
| My Bundle | B999 | 1 |
| Product A | X123 | 5 |
| Product B | Y456 | 4 |

Because My Bundle has a Bundled Quantity of 3 for Product B, and Product B only has 4 Inventory Available, My Bundle's Inventory Available is set to 1.

---

## Notifications, Order Printing, & Packing Slips

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/notifications-and-packing-slip

This allows you to add expiration dates and batch numbers to:

-   [Shopify Notifications](https://www.shopify.com/admin/settings/notifications) (by default does not apply to order confirmation since the email is sent before the batch is assigned)
-   [Order Printer](https://apps.shopify.com/order-printer) and [Shopify Order Printer](https://apps.shopify.com/shopify-order-printer)
-   [Order Printer Pro](https://apps.shopify.com/order-printer-pro)
-   [Multi-Label Barcodes App](https://apps.shopify.com/multi-label-barcodes)
-   And more!

To begin you must enable order notes from the settings page by selecting "Create an order 'additional details' entry for 3rd-party app integration". Once enabled generate a code snippet below for your integration.

## Code Snippet

The resulting code snippet can be added to the appropriate Liquid template for your integration in the location where you want the expiration data displayed. This snippet works **with** the existing template to display expiration data. It is not meant to replace it.

If you do not see your integration in the list and need assistance please contact support.

```liquid
{% comment %}
  Code for the Product Expiration Dates app to display a product's expiration date and related
  informtion in notifications, order printing, & packing slips.

  If you want to hide the expiration date until it's close to a particular number of days
  set the expires_window_days variable below to the number of desired days instead of blank.
  For example:

    {% assign expires_window_days = 30 %}

  For assistance contact support at help@screenstaring.com
{% endcomment %}

{% assign expires_window_days = blank %}

{% capture key %}Expiration Dates {{ line_item.sku }}{% endcapture %}
{% if attributes[key] != blank %}
    {% assign batches = attributes[key] | split: "|" %}
    {% for batch in batches %}
        {% assign batch_data = batch | split: "," %}
        {% assign expires_date = batch_data[0] %}
        {% assign expires_qty = batch_data[1] %}
        {% assign expires_batch = batch_data[2] %}

        {% assign now = "now" | date: "%s" %}
        {% assign seconds_in_a_day = 86400 %}
        {% assign expires_at = expires_date | date: "%s" | plus: seconds_in_day | minus: 1 %}
        {% assign diff = expires_at | minus: now | divided_by: seconds_in_a_day %}
        {% assign show_date = false %}

        {% if expires_window_days == blank  %}
          {% assign show_date = true %}
        {% elsif diff >= 0 and diff < expires_window_days %}
          {% assign show_date = true %}
        {% endif %}

        {% if show_date %}
          {% comment %}
            The date format can be adjust by changing the '%d/%m/%Y' portion below
            to the desired date format codes. See: https://shopify.dev/api/liquid/filters#date
            To use a tranlated date see: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/locales/storefront-locale-files
          {% endcomment %}
          Expires:
          {{ expires_date | date: "%d/%m/%Y" }}

          {% comment %}
            Remove the following if you do not want the quantity and batch name displayed
          {% endcomment %}
          ({{ expires_qty }})
          {% if expires_batch != blank %}
              {{ expires_batch }}
          {% endif %}
        {% endif %}
    {% endfor %}
{% endif %}
```

You may have to change the `line_item` or `line` variable to match what's used in your existing code.

The date format is based on the [Liquid `date` filter](https://shopify.dev/api/liquid/filters#date). It can be adjust by changing the `"%d/%m/%Y"` portion to use the desired date format codes. See the `date` filter's documentation for a list. To use a translated date specify a date format [from your theme's locale files](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/locales/storefront-locale-files). For example, if the format `month_day_year` existed (it may), you can change:

```liquid
{{ expires_date | date: "%d/%m/%Y" }}
```

In the above snippet to:

```liquid
{{ expires_date | date: format: "month_day_year" }}
```

## Technical Details

An attribute will be added to the order for each line item. The attribute will be named `"Expiration Dates [ID]"` where `[ID]` is the line item's: SKU, barcode, or the Shopify variant ID. What is used depends on your store's setup. If you use SKUs it will always be the SKU. If you only use barcode it will be the barcoce, etc...

The attribute's value is a comma-separated string containing the assigned expiration date, quantity, and batch number:

```
2023-04-22,2,BATCH-NUMBER
```

If there are multiple assignments for a line item each assignment will be seperated by the pipe character (`|`):

```
2023-04-22,2,BATCH-NUMBER-1|2023-12-25,1,BATCH-NUMBER-2
```

## Shopify Point of Sale (POS) Integration

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/pos-integration

***Shopify POS integration is only available under the Platinum Plan***

Our Shopify POS integration allows inventory batches to be assigned to orders from within the Shopify POS. To install, add the Product Expiration Dates app as a tile on the POS home screen:

1.  From the POS home screen touch "Add tile" and select "App":

2.  From the app list select "SS: Product Expiration Dates":

3.  Next to "Assign expiration data to products" click "Add":

4.  This will show the "SS: Product Expiration Dates" tile on the home page:

5.  Touch "Save"

Now when items are in the cart you can touch the "SS: Product Expiration Dates" tile and assign inventory batches. Batches shown will be those from the POS' location.

## Entry via Barcode Scanner

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/barcode-scanner

Improve the efficiency of inventory intake and inventory batch assignment by scanning a product's barcode instead of having to search for the product by typing its name, SKU, or barcode.
To get started install [the Barcode Scanner app](https://apps.shopify.com/barcode-scanner-1?utm_source=screenstaring-documention&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=app-link).
The Barcode Scanner app must be used from within [the Shopify Mobile app](https://www.shopify.com/mobile).

## Viewing Order Expiry Dates & Batch Numbers in Shopify

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/viewing-order-expiry-dates-and-batch-numbers

There are several ways to view batch numbers and expiry dates assigned to an order from [the order's page in the Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/orders/manage-orders#view-an-order).

## Admin Block

Adding the Expiration Dates block to the orders page:

1.  Open your order in the [the Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/orders/manage-orders#view-an-order)
2.  On the order's page scroll to the bottom and select "Add block"

3.  Select "Expiration Dates" from the popup menu
4.  This will show the expiration dates assigned to the order's line items, if any. Note that only orders **after** September 11th, 2026 will have their dates shown:

5.  To make the block always appear on the order page click the pin icon:

## Additional Details Section

Batch numbers can be added to the orders page under the Additional Details section:

1.  In the app's settings go to Orders tab
1.  Select "Create an order "additional details" entry with an order's inventory batches"
1.  Click the Update button to save

Inventory batches for new orders will now be added to the order's Additional Details section in the Shopify Admin:

The following information is included:

- `PB123`: the line item SKU
- `B9001`: the batch number assigned to the line item
- `(2)`: the quantity

## Viewing the Order in the App

To open an order's page in the app:

1.  Open your order in the Shopify Admin
2.  On the order's page select "More actions"
3.  Select "Expiration Dates"

---

## Sharing Inventory Between Multiple Stores

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/sharing-inventory

If your inventory supplies multiple stores these stores can be linked. Linking stores allows a singe set of expiration data to be shared across multiple stores.

To link stores you must:

-   Install the app in each store (after the trial period all stores must have an active subscription)
-   Use the same product SKUs in each store (barcode can be used instead, if you prefer)
-   If using locations, use the same location names in each store
-   [Contact support](https://screenstaring.com/#contact) to create the link(s)

---

## Disabled Products

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/disabled-products

If a product is deleted in Shopify but has orders with inventory batches assigned it will become disabled in the app. The prevents it from being processed by future orders while preserving its inventory batch assignment history. If a product is deleted in Shopify and has no inventory batches assigned it will be deleted from the app.

## Sharing Inventory Between Multiple Stores

Sharing inventory between stores relies on unique SKUs or barcodes for inventory batch assignment. If duplicates exist within the app you can disable the unwanted product to prevent it from being processed. This can be done by clicking the Disable button from the product's page in the app.

---

## Expiration Data Metafields

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/expiration-data-metafields

Also see: ***[Notifications, Order Printing, and Packing Slips](https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/notifications-and-packing-slip)***

The Product Expiration Dates app adds metafields to a product's variant(s) under the `expiration_dates` namespace. If the product has no variants the default variant is used.

**Do not add metafield definitions in the Shopify Admin using the `expiration_dates` namespace with any of the below keys.** This is not necessary and prevents the app from functioning correctly. Metafields set by the app are readonly and cannot be set via the Shopify Admin.

If you need to export expiration dates to external applications that only support metafield integration (and do not support JSON metafields) see the `soonest_expiring` key.

The following metafields are available:

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `allocations` | An array of expiration dates and quantities assigned to the variant. The array is sorted by expiration date, soonest to latest so `allocations[0]` will return data for the soonest expiring date. |
| `allocations[N].time` | The expiration date. Format is: `YYYY-MM-DDT00:00`. For example: `2025-01-22T00:00`. Currently the time is always `00:00`. This value can be formatted using the [Liquid `date` filter](https://shopify.dev/api/liquid/filters#date) |
| `allocations[N].quantity` | The remaining inventory quantity |
| `allocations[N].batch_number` | The assigned batch number |
| `allocations[N].location_id` | The Shopify ID of the assigned location |
| `use_within` | An object containing use within information |
| `use_within.use_within_value` | The numeric portion of the use within data. For example, if `30 days` was assigned this will contain `30`. |
| `use_within.use_within_unit` | The unit of time portion of the use within data. For example, if `30 days` was assigned this will contain `days`. |
| `use_within.use_within_value_in_days` | The use within value in days. For example, if `6 months` was assigned, this will contain `180`. We use 30 days per month: 6 \* 30 = 180. |
| `bundled_inventory` | An array of the products that are in the bundle and their expiration data/batch numbers. Only set if the product is a bundle. |
| `bundled_inventory[N].title` | The title of the bundled product |
| `bundled_inventory[N].allocations` | An array of expiration dates and quantities assigned to the variant. Refer to `allocations[N]`'s documentation. |
| `soonest_expiring` | String representation of the soonest expiring inventory batch. Usefull if you need to export expiration dates to external applications that only support metafield integration. Date format can be set on the settings page.
 ***Only available under the Premium Plan*** |

---

## Expiration Data Assigned to an Order

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/expiration-data-orders

Expiration data assigned to orders can be made available to external systems as an order property. An order property is used because Shopify does not support metafields for order line items. To enable this property check "Create an order attribute for an order's inventory batches" from the Orders tab on the settings page.

Orders placed before this option was enabled will not contain the property.

## Order Property Format

Once enabled order attributes named `Expiration Dates SKU` will be added to orders containing expiration data. `SKU` will be replaced with the value of the product's SKU. The attribute's value is in the following format: `BATCH 1|BATCH 2|BATCH 3`.

For example, if you have a product with a SKU of 123 that is assigned a single batch you will have an attribute named `Expiration Dates 123` with a value of: `2024-01-01,1,B123`. Here `2024-01-01` is the assigned expiration date, `1` is the quantity assigned, and `B123` is the batch number.

If the order line has multiple batches they will be included. For example, if SKU 123 was assigned 2 batches, the value would be: `2024-01-01,1,B123|2024-11-21,2,X999`. Here `2024-01-01` is 1 of 2 assigned expiration dates. `1` the quantity assigned and `B123` is its batch number. `2024-11-21` is the other assigned expiration date. `2` is its quantity assigned and `X999` its batch number.

If a batch number (or any value) does not exist its value will be omitted. Here's the multiple batch example without a batch number: `2024-01-01,1,|2024-11-21,2,`

## Parsing the Property's Value

Parsing the value can be done in any language by retrieving the order's attributes via the [Shopify Admin API](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/unstable/queries/order). Here's an example using Liquid:

```liquid
{% assign batches = order.attributes["Expiration Dates 123"] | split: "|" %}
{% for batch in batches %}
    {% assign batch_data = batch | split: "," %}
    {% assign expires_date = batch_data[0] %}
    {% assign expires_qty = batch_data[1] %}
    {% assign expires_batch = batch_data[2] %}

    Expires: {{ expires_date | date: "%d/%m/%Y" }} ({{expires_quantity}})
    Batch {{ expires_batch }}
{% endfor %}
```

---

## API Integration

Source: https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/api-integration

***API integration is only available under the Platinum Plan***

The Product Expiration Dates app provides an API that allows one to manage inventory batches programmatically.

API requests are authenticated using your shop's API key. You can find your API key on the General tab of the settings page. Include your API key in the `X-API-Key` header with each request.

Requests require you to specificy a product or variant identifer. This can be: `sku`, `barcode`, `variant_id`, or Product Expiration Date app ID.

## Base URL

All API endpoints are relative to: `https://apps.screenstaring.com/ed`

### GET `/api/inventories/expiration_dates`

Retrieve inventory batches for a product or variant. You can query by SKU, barcode, or Shopify variant ID

**Query Parameters:**

-   `sku` - The variant's SKU (optional)
-   `barcode` - The variant's barcode (optional)
-   `variant_id` - Shopify variant ID; if a product has no variants use the default variant's ID (optional)
-   `external_location_id` - Filter results by Shopify location ID (optional)

**Example using curl:**

```bash
curl -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" https://apps.screenstaring.com/ed/api/inventories/expiration_dates?sku=PRODUCT-SKU
```

**Response (200 OK):**

```json
[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "expires": "2026-12-31",
    "quantity": 10,
    "batch_number": "BATCH-001",
    "location": {
      "id": 10,
      "external_id": "123456",
      "name": "Main Warehouse"
    },
    "inventory": {
      "id": 789,
      "sku": "PRODUCT-SKU",
      "variant_id": "456789",
      "product_id": "123456"
    }
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "expires": "2027-01-15",
    "quantity": 20,
    "batch_number": "BATCH-002",
    "location": {
      "id": 10,
      "external_id": "123456",
      "name": "Main Warehouse"
    },
    "inventory": {
      "id": 789,
      "sku": "PRODUCT-SKU",
      "variant_id": "456789",
      "product_id": "123456"
    }
  }
]
```

### POST `/api/inventories/expiration_dates`

Create or update an inventory batch. Updates are based on the SKU/barcode combined with either: a) expiration date and location or b) batch number and location. Otherwise, a new batch is created.

**Request Parameters:**

-   `sku` - The variant's SKU (optional)
-   `barcode` - The variant's barcode (optional)
-   `variant_id` - Shopify variant ID; if a product has no variants use the default variant's ID (optional)
-   `expires` - Expiration date, **must be in YYYY-MM-DD format** (required)
-   `quantity` - Quantity available (required)
-   `batch_number` - Batch number (optional)
-   `external_location_id` - The Shopify location ID (required if `location_id` not provided)
-   `location_id` - Product Expiration Dates app ID (required if `external_location_id` not provided)
-   `inventory_batch_assignment_event` - When to assign inventory batches to orders. Only valid when creating a product. Either `"order_placed"` or `"order_item_fulfilled"`. If you're using [Inventory Push](https://help.screenstaring.com/docs/product-expiration-dates/inventory-push) this will always be `"order_placed"`.
-   `invoice_number` - Invoice number (optional)
-   `lot_number` - Lot number (optional)
-   `manufactured_at` - Manufacture date, **must be in YYYY-MM-DD format** (optional)
-   `received_at` - Date received, **must be in YYYY-MM-DD format** (optional)
-   `comments` - Free-form notes (optional)
-   `batch_unit_cost` - Unit cost for the batch (optional)

**Example using curl:**

```bash
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "sku": "PRODUCT-SKU",
    "expires": "2026-12-31",
    "quantity": 10,
    "batch_number": "BATCH-001",
    "id": "9876",
    "external_location_id": "123456"
  }' "https://apps.screenstaring.com/ed/api/inventories/expiration_dates"
```

**Response (200 OK):**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "expires": "2026-12-31",
  "quantity": 10,
  "batch_number": "BATCH-001",
  "location": {
    "id": "9876",
    "external_id": "123456",
    "name": "Main Warehouse"
  },
  "inventory": {
    "id": 789,
    "sku": "PRODUCT-SKU",
    "variant_id": "456789",
    "product_id": "123456"
  }
}
```

### PATCH `/api/inventories/expiration_dates/:id`

Update an existing inventory batch

**URL Parameters:**

-   `:id` - The Product Expiration Dates app ID for the inventory batch (required)

**Request Parameters:**

-   `expires` - Expiration date, **must be in YYYY-MM-DD format** (optional)
-   `quantity` - Quantity available (optional)
-   `external_location_id` - The Shopify location ID (optional)
-   `location_id` - Product Expiration Dates app Location ID (optional)
-   `batch_number` - Batch number (optional)
-   `invoice_number` - Invoice number (optional)
-   `lot_number` - Lot number (optional)
-   `manufactured_at` - Manufacture date, **must be in YYYY-MM-DD format** (optional)
-   `received_at` - Date received, **must be in YYYY-MM-DD format** (optional)
-   `comments` - Free-form notes (optional)
-   `batch_unit_cost` - Unit cost for the batch (optional)

**Example using curl:**

```bash
curl -X PATCH -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "expires": "2027-01-15",
  "quantity": 20,
  "batch_number": "BATCH-002"
}' "https://apps.screenstaring.com/ed/api/inventories/expiration_dates/1"
```

**Response (200 OK):**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "expires": "2027-01-15",
  "quantity": 20,
  "batch_number": "BATCH-002",
  "location": {
    "id": 10,
    "external_id": "123456",
    "name": "Main Warehouse"
  },
  "inventory": {
    "id": 789,
    "sku": "PRODUCT-SKU",
    "variant_id": "456789",
    "product_id": "123456"
  }
}
```

### DELETE `/api/inventories/expiration_dates/:id`

Delete an inventory batch by its ID.

**URL Parameters:**

-   `:id` - The Product Expiration Dates app ID for the inventory batch

**Example using curl:**

```bash
curl -X DELETE -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" https://apps.screenstaring.com/ed/api/inventories/expiration_dates/1
```

**Response (200 OK):**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "expires": "2026-12-31",
  "quantity": 10,
  "batch_number": "BATCH-001",
  "location": {
    "id": 10,
    "external_id": "123456",
    "name": "Main Warehouse"
  },
  "inventory": {
    "id": 789,
    "sku": "PRODUCT-SKU",
    "variant_id": "456789",
    "product_id": "123456"
  }
}
```

## Error Responses

The API returns appropriate HTTP status codes and error messages:

| Status Code | Description | Example Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Bad Request - Missing or invalid parameters | `{"errors": ["param is missing or the value is empty: id"]}` |
| `401` | Unauthorized - Invalid or missing API key | `{"errors": ["Shop not found"]}` |
| `403` | Forbidden - Plan does not allow API access | `{"errors": ["API access not available for your subscription"]}` |
| `404` | Not Found - Product, variant, or location not found | `{"errors": ["Record not found"]}` |
| `422` | Unprocessable Entity - Validation errors | `{"errors": ["Quantity must be greater than 0"]}` |
